articles.description: Strathcona agreed to acquire Greenfire for up to around $2.06 billion, a combination that the Canadian companies said would create an oil sands major that offers faster growth than larger rivals.

articles.title: Hungary's MOL Group Sees Profit Surge on Bumper Refining Margins
articles.description: Hungary's state-backed MOL Group reported around $865 million in net profit for the third quarter, up 143 percent from the same three-month period last year as refining margins soared.

articles.title: Murphy Oil Bets on Israeli Gas Near Leviathan
articles.description: Israel’s Energy Ministry on Monday awarded six offshore natural gas exploration licenses to Houston-based Murphy Oil and Israel’s Ratio Energies, eight months after the war with Iran forced Israel to shut its biggest gas field. The Zone G licenses cover about 1,700 square kilometers of seabed roughly 25 kilometers southwest of Leviathan. Murphy will operate the licenses, and each partner holds 50%. The award marks Murphy’s first venture into the Eastern Mediterranean, and it joins Chevron, the operator of Leviathan and Tamar,…

articles.title: Saudi Pipeline Attacked as OPEC Output Climbs to 90% of Pre-War Levels
articles.description: Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, the kingdom’s main route for moving crude around the Strait of Hormuz, came under attack on Monday, the same day a Reuters survey showed OPEC output had recovered to 90% of its pre-war rate. An Energy Ministry official said the pipeline was targeted in the Medina region, causing a limited fire that emergency crews put out with no casualties and no disruption to operations. The line carries Saudi crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, which handled the bulk of the kingdom’s export growth in October.…

articles.title: Oil Experiences Sharpest Weekly Decline in Months
articles.description: Crude oil experienced its sharpest weekly decline in months on Friday, Ole S. Hansen, Saxo Bank's Head of Commodity Strategy, said in a report sent to Rigzone.

articles.title: Global LNG Markets Face a Winter of Extreme Uncertainty
articles.description: The defining feature of the Northern Hemisphere winter 2026/27 is uncertainty. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices are above $30 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), and gas inventories are markedly lower in key markets. Further price rallies are not a foregone conclusion, though. Potent downside risks remain, including a recovery of Middle Eastern LNG supply and weather-suppressed power and heating demand. articles.title: Europe’s Power Prices Jump to 2022 High as Wind and Solar Falter
articles.description: A weather front is bringing still and cloudy weather at the start of the week in some of Europe’s largest electricity markets, resulting in power prices for peak evening periods soaring to 2022 highs. Across the UK, Germany, and France, the top power markets in Europe, wind and solar power generation is slumping on Monday and is expected to remain below normal until at least the middle of this week. articles.title: Oil prices fall as Trump signals no immediate strikes on Iran
articles.description: Oil prices declined on Monday, 9 November, following comments from US President Donald Trump that suggested a reduced probability of further military action against Iran, reported Reuters.

articles.description: Oil and gas drilling services provider ADES has been awarded contracts by India’s state-controlled oil and gas company Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) to provide two standard jackup rigs in India.

articles.description: Brent crude fell 3.6% to $94.00 per barrel on Monday as Qatar’s prime minister headed to the White House with an Iranian proposal for an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: Iraq's Oil Sales to America Fall to Lowest Since the 2003 War
articles.description: U.S. imports of Iraqi crude oil have slumped this year to a multi-decade low, EIA data show, as the Strait of Hormuz crisis has choked international shipments from OPEC’s second-largest oil producer. U.S. imports have markedly dipped since March, to zero in several weeks this summer, after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz forced Iraq to slash its oil production. articles.title: Nordic Power Prices Could Soar This Winter as Hydropower Reserves Plunge
articles.description: Low water levels in hydropower reservoirs and soaring natural gas prices are putting upward pressure on power prices in the Nordic countries as winter approaches, Denmark-based energy trader Mind Energy says. The surge in gas prices and potentially reduced hydropower generation in southern Norway and Sweden could lead to price spikes this winter, especially if there are prolonged periods of low wind speeds, the analysts said.
